headline: The hose tank learned to speak
lede: Fire Crew's pressure arc drains the tank from four tiles of reach to nothing, but until now the human hose heard only its own spray stop. Tonight it chirps, clunks and blinks — and the never-dry lane proved its weakest title could ship a real fix, not just a report.

notes.text: NEVER-DRY rung (#1571): idle-kick named FIRE CREW 0 weak — its only unowned gap was the #1712 production line, which waits on consented phone takes and can never be lane-faked. The lane marked that bullet decided-state (DISCLAIMER, #2488 doctrine) and shipped a player-visible gameplay fix instead.

sim.js gains TANK_LOW=30 and tankAlarm(level) — a pure rng-free voice: null while the line has muscle, a two-tone caution whose pitch climbs with the drain, a dry-valve clunk at zero. step() names each downward crossing for the hand on the pump only — cpu, seated watch and hydrant refills stay silent.

Proof: firecrewcheck 201 (+22 gates), 4 mutants die by name, firecrewplay +7 legs on real rAF ticks, datasetcheck 84/84 byte-exact. A mid-session rebase over the QA radioDeny lane (#2990) re-validated green before the merge.

Board: fire-crew's README gap list is DISCLAIMER-only now; #2985 (QA) carries the new law's sharp edges — threshold hysteresis, EMPTY naming its cure, a tankStage feature lane at the next #1712 stage.
